def factor_enhanced_regime_aware_reversal(df):
    df_copy = df.copy()
    # Reversal component from parent 1: range expansion reversal
    range_ = df_copy["high"] - df_copy["low"]
    lookback = 50
    mean_range = range_.rolling(lookback, min_periods=lookback).mean()
    std_range = range_.rolling(lookback, min_periods=lookback).std()
    range_z = (range_ - mean_range) / std_range.replace(0, np.nan)
    ret5 = df_copy["close"].pct_change(5)
    raw_reversal = -ret5 * range_z
    # Directional consistency filter with longer lookback (50 days) inspired by parent 1
    ret = df_copy["close"].pct_change()
    up_sum = ret.clip(lower=0).rolling(50, min_periods=50).sum()
    down_sum = (-ret.clip(upper=0)).rolling(50, min_periods=50).sum()
    total_abs = up_sum + down_sum
    direction_ratio = up_sum / total_abs.replace(0, np.nan)
    direction_ratio = direction_ratio.clip(0, 1).fillna(0.5)
    # Attenuate reversal when trend is persistent (high direction ratio)
    regime_weight = 1.0 - direction_ratio
    raw = raw_reversal * regime_weight
    # Smooth with EMA(3)
    signal = raw.ewm(span=3, min_periods=3).mean()
    df_copy["factor_enhanced_regime_aware_reversal"] = signal
    return df_copy["factor_enhanced_regime_aware_reversal"]
description: This crossover factor retains the elite regime-aware reversal mechanism from parent 2 but transfers a single lightweight modification from parent 1: the 50-day lookback window. The directional consistency filter (up-day return ratio) is now computed over 50 days instead of 20, aligning the persistence estimation with the volatility lookback used in the range expansion z-score. When directional consistency is high (persistent trend), reversal signals are dampened; when low (choppy, mean-reverting conditions), reversal signals are amplified. The longer window may capture more stable regime patterns, aiming to improve ICIR and MI while preserving parent 2's strong RankICIR.
